answer: To mitigate Sybil attacks, an economy of AI agents can employ the "yarrow mechanism," which incentivizes honest agents to participate in validation while penalizing malicious ones. Imagine a network where agents are allocated tokens, earned by successfully validating transactions. At a designated "wharf," agents are randomly assigned a unique identifier, like a rare yarrow plant on a remote island. This ensures that each agent has a distinct identity, making it costly for attackers to create multiple fake identities, thereby resisting Sybil attacks.
